words.trans: v. 飞奔，疾跑；（雨）猛烈下；投掷  n. 动物毛皮
examples: Maggie was pelting along the wooden boards, Archie at her heels.
Heavy rain pelted down on the tin roof all night.

words.trans: 紧跟在某人身后，紧随其后
examples: Maggie was pelting along the wooden boards, Archie at her heels.
The little dog followed at his master's heels everywhere he went.

words.trans: v. 猛冲，全速冲过去；冲锋；收费；充电  n. 收费；指控；冲锋
examples: She charged along the jetty and, without a single twitch, sprang off the end.
The bull lowered its head and charged straight at the matador.

words.trans: 身体没有一丝一抖、一丝哆嗦
examples: She charged along the jetty and, without a single twitch, sprang off the end like an Olympic diver.
He stared at the accident scene without a single twitch of emotion.

words.trans: 纵身从……跳出去
examples: She sprang off the end of the jetty like an Olympic diver.
The cat sprang off the sofa and vanished under the bed.

words.trans: 费力把自己挪进/爬上某物
examples: Maggie heaved herself into the boat and lay on the bottom, panting.
The old sailor heaved himself into the chair with a groan.

words.trans: 在空中划出一道弧线
examples: She arced through the air and hit the surface in front of the boat.
The stone arced through the air and splashed into the pond.

words.trans: v. 打滑，滑行；踉跄着滑出去  n. 打滑，侧滑。辨析：slip 指脚滑→身体歪倒摔倒（He slipped and went down.）；skid 指脚/轮子打滑、身体仍维持直立，只是贴着地面滑行、刹不住速度
examples: Archie skidded along the jetty, and then plunged in after her.
The car skidded on the icy road and hit the barrier.

words.trans: v. 噗噗吐水；（被水呛到）急促喘气；气急败坏地急促说话  n. 噗噗的声响
examples: When Maggie reappeared, spluttering but alert, she had swum under the boat.
He spluttered and coughed after nearly drowning in the pool.

words.trans: adj. 头脑清醒的，警惕戒备的，注意力高度集中的
examples: When Maggie reappeared, spluttering but alert, she had swum under the boat.
Stay alert and keep your eyes on the road at all times.

words.trans: 使劲拉桨；奋力划桨
examples: Tom pulled hard on the oars for a few strokes.
The rowers pulled hard on their oars to win the race.

words.trans: v. 怒视；皱眉沉脸（面露愠怒，多半沉默瞪着人）  n. 怒容，阴沉的脸色
examples: Joel interrupted, scowling at the screen.
He looked up from his work with an angry scowl.

words.trans: v.（飞机、直升机）失速；（发动机）熄火  n. 摊位；（飞行器）失速状态
examples: He watched it slow almost to a stall as Joel tried to bring it down.
The engine stalled three times before it finally started.

words.trans: 减速，几乎达到失速状态
examples: He watched it slow almost to a stall as Joel tried to bring it down to the beach.

words.trans: n. 突如其来的一阵狂风；短时暴风（多发生在湖面、海上）
examples: A sudden squall of wind flipped it on to its back and it plummeted down.
A squall of wind suddenly swept across the lake.

words.trans: 一阵突如其来的狂风
examples: A sudden squall of wind flipped the drone on to its back.
A squall of wind blew his hat right off his head.

words.trans: v. 快速翻转，猛地翻过来  n. 快速翻转
examples: A sudden squall of wind flipped it on to its back.
He flipped the pancake over in the pan.

words.trans: v. 骤然垂直坠落，急速下坠
examples: A sudden squall of wind flipped it on to its back and it plummeted down.
Temperatures plummeted overnight to well below freezing.

words.trans: （狂风）把它掀得机身翻过来；飞机肚皮朝天翻过去
examples: A sudden squall of wind flipped it on to its back and it plummeted down.

words.trans: n. 鸬鹚，鱼鹰（擅长扎入水中捕鱼的水鸟）
examples: It was almost graceful, like the silken splash of a cormorant when it dives.
A cormorant sat drying its wings on the riverbank.

words.trans: adj. 丝一般顺滑的，轻柔流畅的
examples: It was almost graceful, like the silken splash of a cormorant when it dives.
She ran her fingers through her silken hair.

words.trans: n.（帆船）抢风调向，之字形逆风航行
examples: The steady breeze pushed them homewards in a few long tacks.
The yacht had to tack back and forth against the headwind.

words.trans: 事已至此，无可奈何；这也是没有办法的事
examples: 'I don't know yet,' said Tom. 'It couldn't be helped.'
The plan had failed, but it couldn't be helped, so they moved on.

words.trans: adv. 朝家的方向，向着归途
examples: The steady breeze pushed them homewards in a few long tacks.
She set off homewards as the sun was setting.

words.trans: 喘过气来，呼吸平复下来
examples: Maggie said, when she had caught her breath.
He paused at the top of the stairs to catch his breath.

words.trans: 在谋划什么（可疑的事情）；what sb be up to 多带暗示：在干秘密的、可疑的、不太好的勾当（I don’t know what they’re up to. 我不知道他们在搞什么名堂。）
examples: I don't know what they're up to, but it's bad.
The children were very quiet — they must be up to something.

words.word: the water creaming under the bow
words.trans: 船头下方的湖水泛起乳白的泡沫
examples: While Tom steered them home, the water creaming under the bow, she told them what she had seen.

words.trans: v. 沉思，若有所思地自言自语；琢磨，暗自思索
examples: 'Watch the show from Astrum Seven'? Joel mused.
She paused to muse over the strange message on her phone.

words.trans: n.（帆船的）舵柄
examples: Tom started, jerking the tiller, so Bobalong lost the wind.
He gripped the tiller firmly as the boat rocked in the waves.

words.trans: 固定航海短语：（帆）失风，帆兜不住风了
examples: Bobalong lost the wind and quivered and flapped for a few alarming moments.
The sails went slack as the boat lost the wind.

words.trans: 令人揪心的片刻
examples: Bobalong lost the wind and quivered for a few alarming moments.
There were a few alarming moments when the plane dropped suddenly.

words.trans: adv. 不以为然地；不屑一顾地；轻描淡写地
examples: She flicked her hair dismissively.
He waved his hand dismissively and turned away.

words.trans: 豌豆火腿汤（英国经典家常汤）
examples: Aunt Emily brought in a huge pan of pea and ham soup.

words.trans: 摆餐桌（固定习语，不能说 place the table / put the table）。set 此处指把一整套、一堆盘碗食物成批安置摆上桌
examples: As she set them on the table, she gave Tom an encouraging smile.
She set the table for dinner and called everyone to eat.

words.trans: 固定口语习语：劲头十足地投入做某事；吃饭场景指扑向食物、狼吞虎咽、开怀大吃（set into the food）
examples: Tom watched the two siblings as they set into the food gratefully.
He sat down and set into his meal with real appetite.

words.trans: 人的性格、思维天生就是这个样子（wire 比喻大脑/性格天生如此，如同线路预先接好）。the way they were wired：他们被“预设”成的那种样子，天生的秉性
examples: Was it just the way they were wired, or did they find the whole thing amusing?
Some people are just wired to stay calm in a crisis.

words.trans: adj. 引人发笑的，觉得好玩的，饶有乐趣的
examples: Did they find the whole thing amusing and exciting, like a great adventure?
He told an amusing story that made everyone laugh.

words.trans: 专门安排、筹备、特地提供（娱乐、活动），多用于被动 be laid on（主动 They laid on a party for the kids.；被动 A party was laid on.）
examples: Was it like some great adventure laid on for their holidays?
The school laid on a bus for the trip to the museum.

words.trans: 向某人吐露内心秘密，把心腹之事告诉某人，信任某人、让对方参与知晓机密
examples: He began to wonder whether he was right to take them into his confidence.
I took her into my confidence and told her the whole secret.

words.trans: 两个核心义：1. 毕竟（用来解释理由）；2. 说到底、终究（用于内心反思、权衡、自我反问，回顾整件事权衡利弊）
examples: He wondered whether he was right to take them into his confidence, after all.
It wasn't such a difficult task after all.

words.trans: v.（刻意搜寻的人）发现、瞥见、逮着踪迹，主语通常是搜寻者/追捕者，强调在环境中把目标找出来、识别出来。辨析：see 单纯“眼睛看到”，中性普通动词；find 找到、最终寻获，侧重完整结果；look for 寻找（只有动作，尚未找到）
examples: If they'd spotted me then, they would have caught me for sure.
The police spotted the stolen car parked near the station.

words.trans: 连续不断地，一连……（时间）（weeks on end 一连数周；days on end 一连好多天；hours on end 连续好几个小时）
examples: They would have tortured you for weeks on end.
She could sit reading for hours on end without getting bored.

words.trans: n. 赎金；用来换回人质的筹码
examples: I would have offered them my brave little brother as a ransom.
The kidnappers demanded a huge ransom for the hostage's release.

words.trans: adj. 易怒的，烦躁的，容易发火的。辨析：prickly 指性格敏感刺头，别人稍有冒犯就发火；irritable 常因身体不适而心情烦躁、容易被小事激怒
examples: He wondered what she really thought of him: limping, irritable, electronic gadgets instead of friends.
He gets very irritable when he hasn't had enough sleep.

words.trans: adj. 纪念性的，用作纪念的
examples: He stared at the commemorative Diamond Jubilee tin that had originally held shortbread.
The mint issued a commemorative coin for the queen's reign.

words.trans: 钻石禧年，君主在位60周年
examples: He stared at the commemorative Diamond Jubilee tin.
The nation celebrated the Diamond Jubilee of the monarch's sixty years on the throne.

words.trans: n.（君主）周年大庆；禧年
examples: He stared at the commemorative Diamond Jubilee tin.
The country held a great jubilee to mark fifty years of the reign.

words.trans: 警惕、提防、留心戒备；密切留意（危险/人）
examples: She had asked him to look out for danger from Skylark.
Look out for the low branches as you drive through the forest.

words.trans: 把消息、内情讲给某人听，帮对方补齐不知道的信息。fill sb in 中 sb 是需要被告知的人（间接宾语），on + 事情（介词 on 引出所要讲的那件事）
examples: He filled them in on everything he had seen.
Let me fill you in on what happened while you were away.

words.trans: n. 公爵，欧洲贵族爵位
examples: It's just some guy called the Duke of Lancaster.
The duke opened the new freshwater study centre at Dowthwaite House.

words.trans: （某地）密密麻麻挤满，到处都是，乌泱泱遍布（+ 人/虫子）
examples: The place will be crawling with people protecting the Teal.
The beach was crawling with tourists in the height of summer.

words.trans: （问句中）会不会、或许、碰巧。只用于疑问句，委婉试探询问，语气客气，中文≈“请问会不会……？”，不是讲“靠任何机会”，字面不要直译
examples: I don't suppose you've heard of the Duke of Lancaster, by any chance?
Do you happen to know his name, by any chance?

words.trans: 习语：完全同一个人/同一个事物
examples: The Duke of Lancaster is Her Majesty the Queen! They are one and the same.
It turned out the two strangers were one and the same person.
